problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(-0.63<Z<0.63).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ | $\,0.6664\,$ | $\,0.6700\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ |

$P(-0.63<Z<0.63)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.63<Z<0.63).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/09754e3068e550f6ba2a457f124828932408d0298ca163d6ad22e1caac51c2d0.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.63<Z<0.63) & =P(Z<0.63)-P(Z\le -0.63) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.63)-P(Z\le -0.63) \\  & =Φ(0.63)-Φ(-0.63).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.63)=0.7357,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(-0.63).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.63) & =P(Z\le -0.63) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.63) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.63) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.63) \\  & =1-Φ(0.63) \\  & =1-0.7357 \\  & =0.2643\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.63<Z<0.63) & =Φ(0.63)-Φ(-0.63) \\  & =0.7357-0.2643 \\  & =0.4714.\end{aligned}
$$
